correctness.rationale: Four standard affine charts cover P1xP1. For each of 4095 nonzero bidegree-(2,3) sections over F2, geometric smoothness is equivalent to all Jacobian ideals (f,fx,fy) being unit ideals; the symbolic source verify_geometry.py uses exact Groebner bases, not rational-only sampling. An independently coded characteristic-two bivariate polynomial/gcd smoothness test reproduced exactly 1116 smooth masks, including all seven of the exhibited net. Independent XOR subspace census yielded 44070 pencils and 250992 pencil/extension incidences; each 3-space has seven pencils and four extension vectors, so 250992/28=8964 distinct nets. Recomputed every net’s 9-point F2-rational spectrum: exactly the stated 14 types with counts summing 8964; independent transformation of all 36 polarized PGL2(F2)^2 automorphisms gave 249 orbits, each size36. A 4-dimensional section subspace has a nonzero kernel of the three-dimensional first-jet evaluation at any rational point, so contains a singular member; the 3-dimensional example proves sharpness. Adjunction gives genus two on smooth (2,3). Exhaustive finite coefficient enumeration is genuine exhaustive proof for this fixed finite vector space, not extrapolation to other fields.

value.rationale: All-smooth linear systems on varieties over finite fields form a motivated extremal problem. A complete census for the first genus-two bi-graded linear system on the smallest split quadric, including every maximal net, projective automorphism orbit and all member point-count spectra, refines generic existence and jet bounds with exact arithmetic geometry. The fixed finite object and orbit invariant are canonical, not a fabricated numerical slice.

limitations: Only polarized split quadric (P1xP1,O(2,3)) over F2; not arbitrary genus-two curves/isomorphism classes.
Combinatorial finite-census algorithms establish a finite fact, not a theorem for larger fields.
